name: 1608 Prairie Avenue — brick house, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 27.250, v -3.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.578 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line. Kept from the district draft (T-2334) by T-2341, which refines the house in place: the main body's rectangle and its rear corner are unchanged.
placement.symbolic_location: 1608 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1608 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle inside the traced outline s20fp-1608-b1 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), kept from the draft. Read in this frame the trace also draws (1) a canted bay on the Prairie face from v 0.0 to 3.7 m, standing 1.07 m proud, and (2) a shallow projection on the south wall from u 9.3 to 13.5 m, about 0.7 m out: the T-1840 census reads both ('a bay on the Prairie face and a small projection on its south wall'), and they are built as the K08 bays in `bays`. (3) A strip about 0.85 m out along the north wall from u 6.2 to 13.0 m that the census does not mention: it is NOT built, and the north wall stands on the rectangle's line; T-2343's or a later reading of the sheet owns it.

stories.note: '2B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 2 full storeys.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick'. T-2341: built as a brick house, front and all — K01's `brick` construction, the K03 common brick on every wall, with stone dressings on the street front.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft's raised principal floor over the basement the sheet's 'B' prints, inside the K01 contract's principal_floor range [0.8, 1.8]; it solves to whole risers of the K07 stoop.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, the principal storey tallest: the draft rules' 3.9 m and a 3.6 m chamber storey (RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md upper 2.9-3.7), raised from the draft's 3.5 so the chamber sashes and the bracketed eave both fit under the soffit. No source reads this house's heights.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A 13-inch brick wall, inside the contract's masonry range [0.23, 0.45]; the sheet prints no wall thickness for this lot.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: Common brick, a 13-inch wall, as the front.

service_wall_brick.note: The sheet colours the house brick; the fabric, bond, heads, string course and grime are the K03 library's common buff brick in common bond (the one panel k03_brick lays), on all four walls since the street front is brick too. No photograph of 1608 has been read, so the brick's colour and bond are the kit's, not the house's.

street_front_trim.note: The street front's window heads from the K09 kit (data/components/prairie_1904/k09_trim.json): a stone lintel under a cornice hood on both storeys, the plainest head the kit carries and the commonest on a brick front of the 1870s on Prairie Avenue; the door keeps K01's flat stone lintel, since K09's one entrance is 1808's Romanesque ring. No source shows 1608's heads.

wall_head.note: The draft's bracketed cornice, kept as the K10 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k10_cornices.json) scrolled timber brackets and bed moulding under the K05 soffit, round all four walls. The draft drew 1608 with a bracketed cornice so its roof would not repeat 1600's two lots north; no source reads it. No cresting: none is read, and an Italianate brick front's low roof is the case for leaving it off.

roof_form.note: A hip roof, the one K01 builds (k01.roof.hip), low-pitched behind the bracketed eave. The draft drew a flat roof behind the cornice and said which roof the house had was T-1859's to decide; no source reads it, and a low hip over a deep plan is the commonest cover on this street's brick houses of the period.

roof_pitch_deg.note: Low, at the foot of the contract's ordinary range [25, 45], as an Italianate eave wants; tinned rather than slated, because K04's Pennsylvania slate is cut for a 45 degree roof.

eave_overhang_m.note: A deep bracketed eave, two feet.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing one door-swing deep before the threshold.

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop half again the door's width.

entrance_bay.note: The trace puts the Prairie-face bay on the SOUTH half of the front (v 0.0-3.7 m of a 6.75 m front), so the door is on the north half. The draft rules row had the entrance south, which the bay would have stood in front of.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 6.75 m front, south to north: the south bay behind the canted bay (its windows are the bay's own), the north bay the door and the chamber window over it.

side_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the south wall, rear to front, clear of the south projection (u 9.4-13.4) and its downpipe.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall.

sash_by_storey.note: Double-hung sash, diminishing upward, inside the contract's sash ranges.

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the front wall, the basement the sheet's 'B' records.

roof_covering.note: Painted tin in standing seams, K04's cover for a roof too low for its slate, with copper ridge and hip rolls and copper flashings. No source reads 1608's roof.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks on the ridge over spine walls between the front and back rooms, as 1808's; no source reads this house's chimneys.

rainwater.note: K04's half-round copper gutter round the eave and round copper downpipes to splash stones: one at the front's north corner (the south half carries the bay), one on the south wall short of the projection, two at the rear corners. All reconstructed.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: The K07 kit's four-panel door under a two-light transom at the head of a straight stone stoop solved from the principal floor. front_yard_m is the street grid's own distance: the draft's front stands 9.00 m behind the Prairie Avenue street line (street_u 28.253 less the 19.25 m body) and the walk begins 1 ft further out (row_66 margin band), 9.31 m.

bays.note: Two K08 bays where the 1911 sheet draws them (T-1840 census s20-1608-f: 'a bay on the Prairie face and a small projection on its south wall'), so their PLACES are inferred from the map; their form is the kit's. FRONT: the kit's canted bay (3.7 m at the wall, 1.1 m out, a 1.5 m face) against a traced bay 3.67 m at the wall and 1.07 m out on the south half of the front, centred 2.6 m from the south corner: 0.76 m north of the traced bay, so that its eaves (2.27 m either side) clear the K10 cornice's corner bracket, which the kit stands 0.20 m from every corner; two storeys under a low tin hip. SOUTH: the kit's full-height projection (4.0 m long, 0.6 m out) against a traced one about 4.2 m long and 0.7 m out, centred 11.4 m from the rear. Their storeys, windows, brick and roofs are reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1608-brick-front-2341).

condition.note: T-2364: the house weathers to its own age on 1904-07-01 from the K14 condition kit (T-2324) rather than wearing K03's fixed full-age soot and damp, on all four of its brick walls and on its stone dressings. BUILT 1886 is a bound, not a date: Robinson's 1886 atlas, plate 10 (robinson_1886_chicago_plate_10), draws a house on lot 5 where this record's main body stands, its outline within the two maps' fits (4.54 m and 3.08 m RMS) of the 1911 sheet's, so the house stood by 1886 and no reading yet says how long before. The kit is evaluated at that bound, the youngest the evidence allows: 18 years standing, age factor 0.45, the same as 1808 Prairie's, so the weathering shown is a floor and an earlier completion year would only darken it. Damp at the wall foot, soot under the soffit, and a trail below every K06 sill and down the wall behind each downpipe, scaled by the fabric (the common buff brick 1.0, the limestone dressings as the kit's dressed trim 1.2). Every layer's value is the kit's reconstruction (L-k14-condition-kit-2324); using the plate's bound as the completion year is this ticket's (L-k14-1608-brick-2364). A building permit, a dated photograph or a directory reading of the house replaces it.

boundary.note: T-3216: no picture of this front is held, so the boundary is a STATED RECONSTRUCTION on the west side of the block's pictured fronts, every one of which closes its street line and gates its walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence on its curb, a pair of entrance gates at the stoop's foot and a gate across the south passage), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (an iron lattice on its base with gate piers at the walk), 1616's boarded street line in the same 1874 plate, and 1638's photograph (iron bars on a stone base between gate piers). Built as the K11 kit's spear fence on its curb, the plainest of them and the block's photographed iron, with the kit's pair of entrance leaves on stone piers, 1.3 m clear on the stoop's centre, standing open (drawn 70 degrees) as 1612's photograph and both pictures of 1620 show their entrance gates. No side gate: the house stands 0.92 m from its south lot line, less than the kit's gate needs between a pier and the wall (0.9 m clear past a 0.5 m pier), so there is no passage to gate and the iron runs unbroken from the lot line to the entrance (K11's T-3216 rule). The street line is parcel prairie_1608's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) carried into this frame, 8.995 m before the front. The lot's sides are the same parcel's, s -0.92 and 7.92. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence's kind, height and line, its gates and their set; liberty L-k11-fences-1600-block-3216.

yard.note: T-3216 (the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door, its gates and its boundaries to their pictures; where no picture shows them, a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of 1608's front is held. The walk is laid on the block's pictured fronts (1612's photograph shows a light paved walk from the public walk through its open entrance gateway to the stoop's foot, and 1616's and 1621's walks are built on it): flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate, the gate's width, to the inner edge of the public walk; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard inside the iron. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, flags, width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; no service walk is built (no picture shows a side passage's floor); liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3216.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2B brick dwelling (D) with a bay on the Prairie face and a small projection on its south wall; no rear building'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2341 (piece 1 of T-1859) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick on all four walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 bays where the sheet draws them, K09 window heads, K10 bracketed cornice, K04/K05 roof — instead of the draft builder. What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '2B', brick, the traced outline with its front bay and south projection) through the T-1840 census. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1608-brick-front-2341. No photograph, plate or description of 1608 has been read; a later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
